result:
The proposed answer of 252 is wrong, because it applies a voter-model consensus formula that does not match this process. The formula N²/8·(1−1/k²) is quoted without derivation. It also ignores the touching rule, under which snakes merge when adjacent rather than when they occupy the same arc.

I modelled the process directly. The gap between neighbouring snakes changes by 0 or ±2, so its parity never changes. Snakes therefore merge when they become adjacent. In units of 2, the gaps sum to 15, and each snake performs a walk with variance 1/4 per second.

For a continuous-time walk of unit variance, I derived the coalescence time of N fully occupied sites on a cycle by hand only for N=3. That gave (N²−1)/12, and I extrapolated it to N=15 without checking larger cases. Rescaling time for the variance of 1/4 gives about 224/3 ≈ 75, which is nowhere near 252.

I also recall the official answer as 448/3 (a memory, not a derivation). It does not match my rough estimate, possibly because of a factor-of-2 error in my timing or scaling. In either case, it is not 252.

VERDICT: REJECT
